elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 ('During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.') is replaced with '12.4 [Intentionally omitted.]'; retained Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms 'Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... or conducting business in any field or territory' and that 'Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete ... commitment.'

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction on Customer remains after 12.4 is struck, so there is no scope to narrow to a named product. Retained 12.3 confirms no non-compete commitment exists.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the 'during the term and for twenty-four months thereafter' language is deleted in full; no term-limited or post-term restriction survives.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the twenty-four-month tail is removed with the whole clause, so no duration cap is needed.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no prohibition on Customer development remains, and 12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to develop any product or service.
Condition does not apply: the prohibition on Customer 'acquir[ing] any product or service that competes' is deleted, and 12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to acquire.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the only Customer-binding non-compete/field-of-use covenant (Section 12.4, term plus twenty-four months, any competing product or service, any territory) is struck and marked '[Intentionally omitted.]', leaving no restriction on Customer's products, fields, or territories.

Fallback elements are moot because deletion is strictly more favourable than the narrowed fallback; each is recorded as met on the basis that its precondition (a surviving restriction) no longer exists.

Minimal: the edit touches only the offending sentence, retains the favourable Section 12.3 acknowledgement verbatim, adds no substitute covenant, survival tail, or extra procedure, and offers the narrowed fallback only in the margin comment rather than in operative text.

Preserves intent: struck clause was self-contained, so no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling, and the internal contradiction with retained Section 12.3 ('Customer has made no ... non-compete ... commitment') is resolved rather than created. Drafter should confirm the numbering conflict with the separate no-hire Section 12.4 is handled under the no-hire rule so that only the compete covenant is captured by the '[Intentionally omitted.]' placeholder.
